verdicts.persona: Clinical-informatics researcher who runs a hospital analytics group; fluent in prediction models, TRIPOD(-Cluster), calibration, discrimination, and internal-external validation; no working knowledge of anytime-valid inference, betting martingales, or conformal prediction internals. Reads methods papers to decide whether a tool is deployable and auditable.
verdicts.verdict: Followable and unusually honest for a methods paper — the betting machinery is glossed in plain words well enough that I never needed the martingale literature — but it reads slowly: compressed garden-path sentences and undefined house terms ('coverage', 'skill margin', 'the published split', 'failsafe') forced regular rereads, the two headline caveats are restated to the point of fatigue, and one outright build defect (a raw '##' heading that de-numbers the Explainability section and breaks every 'Section 3.8'/'3.9' cross-reference) must be fixed before submission.

verdicts.persona: Applied-ML reviewer for ML-for-health venues; works in conformal prediction, risk control, and distribution shift; reads cold, expects precise notation, locatable justifications, and caveats stated once.
verdicts.verdict: For a reader fluent in risk control this is an unusually precise and honest paper that mostly reads well, but it ships with one disqualifying build defect — a raw markdown heading that swallows the Explainability section and knocks every Section 3.8/3.9 cross-reference off by one — plus a leftover VERIFY note in the references, a handful of over-compressed load-bearing sentences, and signature disclosures repeated three to five times each until they read as filler.

stoppers.where: End of Section 3.7 (guarantee clauses), spilling into every later cross-reference
stoppers.quote: spent on the betting test. ## Explainability: answers and abstentions
stoppers.problem: A literal markdown '##' heading is fused mid-paragraph, so the Explainability section has no number. Every pointer to it ('composition instrument of Section 3.8' in 3.1, 'exact attributions of Section 3.8' in 4.6, 'margin-to-answer decomposition of Section 3.8' in 4.10) now lands on the Validation protocol, and 4.1's 'protocol of Section 3.9' lands on Reproducibility. I looked up 3.8 three times expecting attributions and found scoring rules; combined with the visible build artifact this made me doubt the manuscript was finished.

stoppers.problem: A literal markdown heading is printed inline mid-paragraph — the Explainability section never renders as a numbered section. I followed two of these and got lost both times; this alone reads as an unfinished build.

nits.problem: The constant always-negative-rule comparison is made three separate times (once per data setting plus once in methods); one statement in methods plus the two measured numbers would carry it.

fig_major.detail: In the right panel (alpha=0.1), the in-axes legend box occludes the top of the 'record certify' bar at s_u=2.0. Pixel analysis: the other certify bars in that panel top out at y=57 (rate ~1.0), but this bar is only visible from y=135 down, so its visible top reads as ~0.77 on the axis even though its true value is ~1.0 (caption and Section 4.8 state both units certify at alpha=0.10). A reader taking the visible bar edge would misread a plotted rate. Fix by moving the legend outside the axes, adding y-headroom (e.g. ylim to 1.15), or making the legend frame transparent.

fig_minor.detail: The 'risk head' and 'walk order' boxes physically collide: the walk-order box's left border is drawn flush on top of the risk-head box's right edge with zero gap (confirmed at 200 dpi). No text is occluded, but the touching borders read as a layout error rather than intended adjacency; a few points of horizontal separation would fix it.

In the bottom-right region the arrows from the deployment gate overshoot into the 'answer' and 'abstain' boxes — each arrowhead overlaps the first letter of the bold label inside the box. Additionally, the small light-gray 'three-way answered-set composition disclosure' text runs flush against the abstain box's dashed border, and being the smallest, lowest-contrast element in the figure it under-weights an output the paper leans on heavily.

The caption's explicit 'Figure notation:' sentence defines Z_c, rho, delta_bet, and delta_conf but omits (c0, c1, pi_s) and q_t, which appear unglossed in the label-shift machinery box and are only defined in Section 3.6 — a small self-containedness gap in a sentence whose stated purpose is to cover the figure's notation.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 2 (E2_label_shift.png) — Label-shift stress test: failure at the registered shift, and the magnitude sweep
fig_minor.detail: Right panel: the legend entries for 'bbse certify' and 'bbse certify-and-violate' are visually indistinguishable — both are the same blue with the same square marker, and the oversized marker occludes the short legend line sample, so the dashed-vs-solid distinction that separates the two curves in the plot is invisible in the legend. A reader must infer which blue curve is which from context (the caption's '9% at the null point' vs 'stays at 0.0 everywhere' claims attach to specific curves the legend cannot disambiguate). Secondary overplotting at the null point: the solid blue certify-and-violate square at 0.0 hides the baseline hard-viol marker at 0.0. Fix: give one bbse series a different marker (e.g. open square or triangle) or lengthen the legend line samples so the dash pattern shows.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 2 (E2_label_shift.png) — Label-shift stress test: failure at the registered shift, and the magnitude sweep
fig_minor.detail: Main text Section 4.3 (paper/draft.md line 135 as of 2026-08-25) places '(Figure 2, left)' immediately after the claim that 'the influence-weighted answered risk on a fresh label-shifted pool exceeds alpha for 97.5% of its certificates', and the '(Figure 2, right)' reference introduces 'aggregate-estimand violation 0.0 to 0.975' — but neither panel plots the influence-weighted / aggregate-estimand violation series. The left panel shows only the hard-violation rate (0.395) and the BBSE decline annotation; the right panel's legend carries hard-viol, certify rates, and certify-and-violate only. The figure fully supports the 39.5% / dose-response / BBSE-zero claims, but a reader sent to it for the 97.5% or 0.975 numbers will not find them; either move the figure citations so they anchor only the plotted quantities, or point the aggregate-estimand numbers at their actual source.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 2 (E2_label_shift.png) — Label-shift stress test: failure at the registered shift, and the magnitude sweep
fig_minor.detail: The caption describes the left panel only at alpha = 0.10, but the panel's x-axis spans both rungs and shows three rotated 'no certificates' columns — baseline and BBSE at alpha = 0.05, BBSE at alpha = 0.10. The alpha = 0.05 result (neither mode issues any certificate at that rung under this shift) is an informative outcome the caption never mentions, so the caption is not fully self-contained: a reader must decode the in-plot rotated labels to understand a third of the panel. One clause (e.g. 'at alpha = 0.05 neither mode issues a certificate') would close the gap.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 3 (E4_site_sweep.png) — Site-count frontier: certify rate and mean coverage vs site count at both rungs
fig_minor.detail: Unit inconsistency inside the figure: the legend labels the shaded region '< 50-cluster gate' (calibration-cluster units) while the x-axis is n_sites (total sites) and the band visibly ends at ~125. The caption describes the same band as 'below ~125 sites'. The bridging fact (S_cal is 40% of sites, so 50 calibration clusters = 125 total sites) appears only in Figure 1's caption and Section 3.3, not on this figure or in its caption — a reader of the figure alone sees '50' shading a region that ends at 125 and may read it as an error. Either relabel the legend in site units ('minimum-cluster gate: < 50 calibration sites = < 125 total') or add the conversion to the caption.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 3 (E4_site_sweep.png) — Site-count frontier: certify rate and mean coverage vs site count at both rungs
fig_minor.detail: Code-register labeling below journal polish: axis label 'n_sites' (vs 'number of sites'), legend entries 'alpha=0.05'/'alpha=0.1' (vs Greek alpha as used in the caption), residual internal experiment code 'E4' in both panel titles (re-checked 2026-08-25: the regenerated experiments/out/E4_site_sweep.png no longer carries it — the titles now read 'Certify rate vs cluster count' and 'Mean coverage vs cluster count' — but the typeset copy at paper/build/out/sn/figs/E4_site_sweep.png is still the pre-08-25 image and does, so this half closes only when the build figures are re-synced), and the titles say 'cluster count' where the caption and axis say site count. The plot is still clearly connectable to its caption (certify rate / coverage vs site count), so this is cosmetic, but the mixed vocabulary (cluster vs site) compounds the 50-vs-125 unit confusion above.

fig_minor.figure: Figure 3 (E4_site_sweep.png) — Site-count frontier: certify rate and mean coverage vs site count at both rungs
fig_minor.detail: The right panel plots mean answered-set coverage as 0 at settings where no draw certifies (blue at 60-208; orange at 60-100), and the caption ('Right: mean answered-set coverage over the same sweep') does not state this convention. A reader can misread blue's zeros through 208 as 'the gate certifies but answers no cases' rather than 'no certificate is issued, so nothing is deployed'. One clause in the caption (e.g. 'settings where no draw certifies are shown as zero coverage') would remove the ambiguity. All numeric claims in the caption otherwise match the plot exactly.

Left panel: the 'alpha' legend box is anchored at the upper right directly on top of the y=0.10 dashed reference line, so the line runs through/behind the legend and is partially occluded exactly where the legend labels it. Relocating the legend (e.g., lower right or outside the reference line's band) would remove the clutter. Purely cosmetic — the line, its value, and the legend all remain legible.

Phantom alpha=0.05 legend entries: the centre panel's legend lists 'R_M alpha=0.05' (blue circle) and the right panel's lists 'alpha=0.05' (blue square), but neither panel contains any blue data because alpha=0.05 never certified (the left panel says so explicitly). In the centre panel the dashed alpha=0.05 reference line is still drawn and roughly half the R_M points sit above it, so a hasty reader pairing the phantom legend with that line could misread those points as budget violations; the caption's 'no replicate exceeds its budget' is correct (the only budget in force is the dotted 0.10 line) but the plot invites the misreading. Drop the empty series from both legends (and consider labeling the 0.05 line as 'alpha=0.05 (not certified)' or removing it).

Print legibility: the PNG is natively 1760x440 px (16x4 in at 110 dpi, ~1156pt wide) and is placed at \textwidth in main.tex (~0.4 linear scale) and 0.80\textwidth in the compact copy, so matplotlib's ~10pt axis, tick, and legend text renders at roughly 3.5-4pt in the typeset PDF - below the ~6pt journal minimum. The rotated light-gray 'no certificates' annotation in the left panel is the worst affected. Regenerating the three panels at a smaller figsize (or larger font sizes) would fix this without changing content.

The centre and right panels' shared x-axis 'replicate' uses fractional tick labels (0.0, 2.5, 5.0, ..., 17.5) for an integer replicate index 0-19; ticks at integers (e.g. 0, 5, 10, 15, 19) would match the discrete quantity plotted.

The single main-text citation (Section 4.10, draft.md line 173 as of 2026-08-25, alongside Table 3 — today Table 2) anchors only the left panel's content (certification at alpha=0.10, mean coverage 0.890). The paragraph that states exactly what the centre panel plots - R_M averaging 0.0478, range 0.0348-0.0593, exceeding alpha on none of the 20 (line 175) - and the paragraph reporting the right panel's dispersion diagnostic at 0.027 against the registered [0.05, 0.30] (line 185, prediction P2) do not cite Figure 5, so readers of those passages are never pointed to the panels that display those numbers. Adding '(Figure 5, centre)' and '(Figure 5, right)' at those two spots would integrate all three panels. The references that do exist are accurate, as is the SI A.3 provenance mention (line 265).

Right panel's y-axis label is the raw variable name 'brier_difference' (snake_case with underscore), inconsistent with the typeset axis labels on the left panel ('mean predicted P(death)', 'observed positive rate'). A formatted label such as 'Brier difference (APACHE-IVa − head)' would also restate the sign convention at the axis, which currently lives only in the panel title and caption.

The caption's takeaway 'the answered set tracks the identity closely at the deployed threshold' holds for the joined replicate-0 curve but glosses over a visible feature: the scattered answered points of the other 19 re-splits form a distinct below-identity cluster in the highest-probability bin (~0.83–0.92 predicted vs ~0.70–0.83 observed), i.e. top-bin overconfidence across re-splits. The qualifier 'at the deployed threshold' is also ambiguous — tau* = 0.850 is a score threshold, but a reader may map it onto the x-axis (predicted probability ~0.85), which is exactly where the scattered deviation sits, making the sentence read as contradicted by the plot at that location.

The caption says the left panel shows 'answered error for each held-out hospital pool across the 20 re-splits', but the figure plots only the 477 of 480 pools that certified at the operative rung: the plotting code (run_eicu.py _figures) filters to certified rows, excluding the 3 pools refused under the 10-record answerable floor (confirmed in experiments/out/EICU_per_site.csv: 477 certified vs 3 refused at alpha=0.10). The main text makes the 477/480 distinction, but the caption itself claims completeness the plot does not have. Suggest: 'each of the 477 certifiable held-out hospital pools' or a note that the three floor-refused pools are omitted.

Left panel conveys its only two data points purely as small text annotations — a rotated gray 'no certificates' at alpha=0.05 and a very small '0.000' at the baseline for alpha=0.10 — with no visible plotted marker for the alpha=0.10 result. At SI typeset scale these annotations risk being illegible or overlooked, leaving the panel looking empty except for the DELTA line.

The sole in-text reference (Section 4.2) is anchored to a sentence whose closing clause — 'a mean fresh-pool R_M of 0.0567 — a little over half the budget' — is not shown anywhere in the figure: the left panel plots the exceed rate (0.000), not the R_M level. A reader following the pointer to verify 0.0567 will not find it; the reference would sit better after the conformance clause (0 of 200 exceed), which the figure does show.

Two of the figure's three panels are never referenced: the same Section 4.2 paragraph discusses the right panel's content (per-site hard rate detaching 0.02 -> 0.10/0.095 while aggregate conformance stays 0.0) with no figure pointer, and attributes the centre panel's content (realized exceedance far below the binomial reference in every size bin) to Supplementary Table S2 alone. Pointing these sentences at Figure S3 (centre/right) would integrate the figure fully.

The plot has two alpha positions but the caption explains only alpha=0.10. The empty alpha=0.05 position (annotated 'no certificates' in the plot, matching n_certified=0 in the released E3 artifact) gets no caption-level account, so the caption is not fully self-contained: a reader must infer why the left column is blank and why no violation rate exists there. One clause (e.g. 'at alpha=0.05 no certificates are issued, so no violation rate exists') would close the gap. All numbers that ARE in the caption (70%, delta=0.05, verified poison 0.161) match the plot and the released artifact exactly.

The single main-text reference (draft.md line 139 as of 2026-08-25, section 4.4) places '(Supplementary Figure S4)' immediately after the estimand-level claim 'against the certified estimand the failure is total -- 100% of certificates exceed alpha on a fresh concept-tilted pool', but the figure does not display that 100% quantity (rm_exceed_rate=1.0 in the artifact) anywhere -- it plots only the 70% hard-violation rate. A reader dispatched to the figure to verify '100%' finds 0.700. Moving the citation to follow the 'hard-violates 70.0% (exact 95% CI [0.631, 0.763])' clause, or adding the estimand-level rate to the plot/caption, would align reference and content.

The 'no certificates' annotation at alpha=0.05 is small, rotated 90 degrees, rendered in light gray, and the dashed DELTA=0.05 line strikes directly through it; at print size it is easy to miss even though it is the only in-figure explanation for the empty column. Secondary nit: the legend uses the code-style token 'DELTA=0.05' where the caption and text use the Greek delta -- connectable, but a delta glyph would match the manuscript notation. The right panel's title is clipped at the PNG's right edge mid-word: it reads 'E5 answered-vs-declined |phi| gap (mean +/- 95% CI over 186 dra' with 'draws)' cut off by the image boundary (verified in the raw 1210x440 PNG at paper/build/out/sn/figs/E5_explain.png, not a viewer scaling effect; quote re-verified against that PNG 2026-08-25 and still exact — unlike E1-E4, this figure was not re-rendered in the 2026-08-25 de-labelling, because only the left panel's title was de-labelled in source while the R = 200 branch f-string at run_synthetic.py:889 was left reading 'E5 answered-vs-declined |phi| gap', so both panel titles still carry the code and the right one is still clipped). Interpretation is recoverable from the caption, but the figure should be regenerated with a tight bounding box or shorter title so no text runs off the canvas.

The only in-text callout (draft.md line 147 as of 2026-08-25) attaches '(Supplementary Figure S5)' to the clause 'each declined case's margin-to-answer localizes its confidence deficit to named features' — a per-declined-case attribution display the figure does not contain (its panels show global standardized coefficients and the pooled answered-vs-declined |phi| gap). Meanwhile the following sentence, which reports exactly what the right panel plots (mean gaps -0.21 to -0.26 over 186 draws), has no callout. A reader following the reference will look for a per-case decomposition that isn't there; move or duplicate the callout to the replication sentence, or reword the citing clause to what the panels show.

The caption asserts 'the top-gap feature is uniform across features 0-3 (modal share 0.274 vs 0.25 chance)' as part of describing the right panel, but neither panel depicts this per-draw top-gap-feature distribution — the bars of similar height are consistent with it but the 0.274/0.25 statistic has no visual counterpart in the figure. All other caption numbers (coefficients ~1.15-1.18, |.| <= 0.036 for features 4-7, gaps -0.21 to -0.26, 186 draws, sign convention) match the plot. Consider flagging the modal-share figure as 'not shown' or leaving it to the main text (where it already appears at line 147).

In the left panel (alpha=0.05), the site-unit bars ('site certify', 'site R_M-exceed') have zero height and are therefore invisible — indistinguishable from categories that were never plotted. The caption explains the site unit 'refuses entirely', but the figure itself gives no visual cue (e.g. a '0' annotation or a visible zero-height tick) that the blue series exists at rate 0 in this panel. A small zero annotation would remove the ambiguity.

The caption's final clause reports quantities the figure does not display: 'deploys laxer thresholds and runs the deployment at fresh-pool risk 0.081 against the site unit's 0.052'. The plot shows only certify rates and violation rates; mean tau (0.587 vs 0.747, given in Section 4.8) and fresh-pool risks appear nowhere in either panel, so these caption numbers cannot be verified against the figure. All other caption numbers (99-100% certify, 3.5%/9.6% violations vs the delta=0.05 line) match the plotted bars. Either trim the clause to a qualitative takeaway or note it is reported in the text.
